Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Parvesh Kumar Pandey,Sarvesh Kumar Pandey
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A. 
Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.

2.  The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C., has been filed for quashing the Non Bailable Warrant order dated 16.05.2022, passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Varanasi in Criminal Case No. 765 of 2010, titled as State v. Kamlesh and others, arising out of case crime no.
104 of 1998, under Sections 420, 272 IPC and Section 25, 52, 64, 69 Forest (Conservation) Act,
1980, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954, registered at P.S. Adampur, District Varanasi.
3.
Learned counsel for applicants submits that impugned order is against the facts and law.

The applicants had no knowledge about the proceedings initiated against them due to which they could not appear on the date fixed by the trial Court, hence, non-bailable warrant was issued against the applicants.
4. Per contra learned A.G.A has opposed.

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the matter, it is directed that in case the applicants appear and move appropriate application before the trial Court for recalling the non bailable warrant, the same shall be decided expeditiously in accordance with law.
For a period of 25 days or till the applicant move an application before the trial Court, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants.
Further, the Court shall not entertain the fictitious and repetitive personal exemption application, and if filed, the same shall be dismissed with reasonable costs.
6. The application is disposed of accordingly.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Considering the facts and circumstances of the matter, it is directed that in case the applicants appear and move appropriate application before the trial Court for recalling the non bailable warrant, the same shall be decided expeditiously in accordance with law.
For a period of 25 days or till the applicant move an application before the trial Court, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants.
Further, the Court shall not entertain the fictitious and repetitive personal exemption application, and if filed, the same shall be dismissed with reasonable costs.
6. The application is disposed of accordingly.
